| f1 | defect | CRITICAL | AC3 SAYS SUPERSEDE IS NARROW. IT IS NOT, IN PRODUCTION.<br><br>CLAIM: the legacy signature is `pane_pipe=1 AND marker empty AND ~/.pij/pane-signals/_&lt;N&gt;.raw exists`. On the operator's real tmux server it is constant-true, so the conjunction degenerates to `pane_pipe=1 AND marker empty` — which is exactly the condition the plan promises will still be REFUSED.<br><br>PROOF, measured on this machine just now, not reasoned:<br>  live panes: 69<br>  live panes with a ~/.pij/pane-signals/_&lt;N&gt;.raw file: 69<br>  live panes with a file: 69/69 = 100%<br>And decisively, the file does not even imply a legacy PIPE:<br>  panes with pane_pipe=0 that nevertheless have the sink file: 31<br>  (e.g. %0, %14, %15, %16, %17, %18, %45, %50, %51, %56, %57, %63, %778, %1960, %1962, %2084-%2087, %2347 — all size 0)<br>The legacy daemon creates `_&lt;N&gt;.raw` for every pane it ENUMERATES, not for every pane it TAPS. Existence of the file is therefore evidence about the legacy daemon's pane inventory, never about who owns the current pipe.<br><br>FAILURE SCENARIO, concrete and reachable today: 13 live panes right now have pane_pipe=1 with NO @pij-tap-sink marker. Any pane a person or another tool pipes with a plain `tmux pipe-pane -O -t %N 'cat &gt;&gt; /somewhere/mine.raw'` lands in exactly that state. Adopt that pane into rs and the new arm fires: rs runs `pipe-pane -t %N`, silently destroying a foreign capture it was explicitly promised to refuse. The refusal arm below it is unreachable for any pane the legacy daemon has ever seen.<br><br>WHY THE LIVE PROOF MISSED IT: assets/live-proof.md's foreign-pipe check piped %3169 'under a foreign MARKER'. A foreign marker exits at the marker_matches test, one arm ABOVE the new code. The unmarked foreign case — the only one the new arm can reach — was never run live.<br><br>SMALLEST FIX: make the third conjunct prove ASSOCIATION rather than existence. The PM already used the right instrument by hand in the AC1 transcript: `pgrep -af 'pane-signals/_3169.raw'` returned PID 59681. Require a live process whose command line names that exact legacy sink path before superseding. That is one extra check in has_legacy_tap_sink, it fails closed (no writer found -&gt; refuse), and it makes the predicate mean what its name says. | f3 | defect | MEDIUM | next_retry_at IS GATED ON A FACT THAT DOES NOT DECIDE RETRY, AND IS A CONFIG ECHO OF THE ONE THAT DOES.<br><br>The PM named this as their least-confidence item and was right to. Three separate ways the field misreports:<br><br>1. WRONG PREDICATE. `next_retry_at` is emitted iff `recipient.pane.is_some()`. Pane presence has nothing to do with whether a row is on a retry cadence. A BOUND PANELESS socket seat whose transport returns Queued is retried by the drain on every single tick (worker.rs:207 `let Some(pane) = ... else { return self.release_or_backoff(...) }` -&gt; release_body -&gt; `retry(job, Duration::ZERO)`), and its receipt reports next_retry_at: null. A row that IS retried says it has no retry time.<br><br>2. CONFIG ECHO, NOT A MEASUREMENT. The value is `at + delivery_interval_secs`, read from Config, never from the enqueued job. The persisted schedule is `retry(job_id, Duration::ZERO)` — not_before is NOW. So the row is eligible immediately and is picked up by whichever tick comes next, which may be 100ms away or a full interval away depending on tick phase. This is the classic shape where reported and observed agree in every ordinary test because the test clock and the config are the same number: delivery/mod.rs's fixtures hardcode retry_interval_ms: 1_000 and assert next_retry_at == 2_234, i.e. they assert the arithmetic, not the schedule. No test can currently fail if the drain's real cadence and the config diverge.<br><br>3. THE DOC COMMENT IS BACKWARDS. model.rs:621 says 'Earliest scheduled retry'. Because not_before is ZERO, the earliest scheduled retry is the next tick; the value emitted is an UPPER bound on it. A consumer that sleeps until next_retry_at before re-checking is correct-by-accident; one that treats it as 'nothing will happen before this' is wrong.<br><br>FAILURE SCENARIO: an operator or UI polls a queued receipt for a paneless bound socket seat, sees next_retry_at: null, and concludes the row is parked pending human action — while the daemon is in fact retrying it every 5 seconds. The inverse for an operator-hold row on a pane seat: it reports a retry timestamp for a row whose release depends on the operator, not on a timer.<br><br>SMALLEST FIX: read it from the row instead of computing it. `enqueue_delivery` already returns the job; surface its not_before and emit `next_retry_at = not_before` (i.e. `at`) whenever the row is genuinely on the drain, gated on 'this row will be drained', not on 'the seat has a pane'. If reading not_before is too wide for this plan, the one-line honest version is to gate on the same condition the drain uses and correct the doc comment to 'no earlier than'. Either way add ONE test where the config interval and the drain cadence differ, so the echo can fail. | crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:131 (queued_outcome) and crates/core/src/model.rs:621 (the field's doc comment) | — | — | — | — | — | — |

This MATCHES AC3 as written ('once per pane per daemon boot'), so it is not a finding. Two behaviours worth knowing you chose: (a) a refusal that recurs after a real intervening remediation is silent forever, so the operator's fix is unconfirmable from the log; (b) keying on the error STRING means any pane whose refusal text varies (paths, ids) logs more than once, which is the AC's promise leaking in the other direction. If either matters, key on pane_id alone and clear the entry whenever that pane is observed healthy. |

They differ today only because rs's state dir is ~/.pij-rs and legacy's is ~/.pij. A deployment pointed at --state-dir ~/.pij would make rs read its OWN sinks as the legacy signature. A one-line assertion at the composition root closes it permanently. |
